metadata.chapter_title: Best-Fit Subspaces and Singular Value Decomposition (SVD)

nodes.name: Best-fit line for a probability density
nodes.statement: If $p$ is a probability density in $d$-space, the best fit line for $p$ is the direction $\mathbf{v}_1 = \arg\max_{|\mathbf{v}|=1} E_{\mathbf{x} \sim p}[(\mathbf{v}^T \mathbf{x})^2]$.

nodes.name: Best-fit $k$-dimensional subspace for a density
nodes.statement: If $p$ is a probability density in $d$-space, the best-fit $k$-dimensional subspace is $V_k = \arg\max_{\dim(V)=k} E_{\mathbf{x} \sim p}(|\mathrm{proj}(\mathbf{x}, V)|^2)$.

nodes.name: The Greedy Algorithm Works
nodes.statement: For each $k$, the subspace $V_k$ spanned by the first $k$ singular vectors $\mathbf{v}_1, \ldots, \mathbf{v}_k$ of $A$ is the best-fit $k$-dimensional subspace for $A$.
assumptions: $A$ is an $n \times d$ matrix with singular vectors $\mathbf{v}_1, \ldots, \mathbf{v}_r$
conclusions: For each $1 \leq k \leq r$, $V_k = \mathrm{span}(\mathbf{v}_1, \ldots, \mathbf{v}_k)$ is the best-fit $k$-dimensional subspace

nodes.statement: By induction on $k$. Choose orthonormal basis of any best-fit $W$ so that $\mathbf{w}_k \perp \mathbf{v}_1, \ldots, \mathbf{v}_{k-1}$. Then $|A\mathbf{w}_i|^2 \leq |A\mathbf{v}_i|^2$ for each $i$.

nodes.name: Frobenius norm and singular values
nodes.statement: For any matrix $A$, the sum of squares of the singular values equals the square of the Frobenius norm: $\sum \sigma_i^2(A) = \|A\|_F^2$.
assumptions: $A$ is a real matrix with singular values $\sigma_1, \ldots, \sigma_r$

nodes.statement: Since $\mathbf{v}_1, \ldots, \mathbf{v}_r$ span the row space, $\sum_i (\mathbf{a}_j \cdot \mathbf{v}_i)^2 = |\mathbf{a}_j|^2$ for each row $\mathbf{a}_j$. Summing over rows gives the result.

nodes.name: Matrix equality via vector products
nodes.statement: Matrices $A$ and $B$ are identical if and only if $A\mathbf{v} = B\mathbf{v}$ for all vectors $\mathbf{v}$.
assumptions: $A$ and $B$ are matrices of the same dimensions
conclusions: $A = B$ iff $A\mathbf{v} = B\mathbf{v}$ for all $\mathbf{v}$

nodes.statement: Apply both matrices to standard basis vectors $\mathbf{e}_i$; $A\mathbf{e}_i$ is the $i$-th column of $A$.

nodes.name: SVD Decomposition
nodes.statement: Any $n \times d$ matrix $A$ with right-singular vectors $\mathbf{v}_i$, left-singular vectors $\mathbf{u}_i$, and singular values $\sigma_i$ satisfies $A = \sum_{i=1}^r \sigma_i \mathbf{u}_i \mathbf{v}_i^T$.
assumptions: $A$ is an $n \times d$ matrix of rank $r$
conclusions: $A = \sum_{i=1}^r \sigma_i \mathbf{u}_i \mathbf{v}_i^T = U D V^T$

nodes.statement: Show $\sum_i \sigma_i \mathbf{u}_i \mathbf{v}_i^T \mathbf{v}_j = \sigma_j \mathbf{u}_j = A\mathbf{v}_j$ by orthonormality. Extend to all $\mathbf{v}$ and apply Lemma 3.3.

nodes.name: Rows of $A_k$ are projections
nodes.statement: The rows of $A_k = \sum_{i=1}^k \sigma_i \mathbf{u}_i \mathbf{v}_i^T$ are the projections of the rows of $A$ onto the subspace $V_k$ spanned by the first $k$ singular vectors.
assumptions: $A_k = \sum_{i=1}^k \sigma_i \mathbf{u}_i \mathbf{v}_i^T$ is the rank-$k$ truncated SVD of $A$
conclusions: Rows of $A_k$ are projections of rows of $A$ onto $V_k$

nodes.statement: Projection of row $\mathbf{a}$ onto $V_k$ is $\sum_{i=1}^k (\mathbf{a} \cdot \mathbf{v}_i)\mathbf{v}_i^T$. In matrix form this is $\sum_{i=1}^k A\mathbf{v}_i \mathbf{v}_i^T = \sum_{i=1}^k \sigma_i \mathbf{u}_i \mathbf{v}_i^T = A_k$.

nodes.name: Best rank-$k$ Frobenius norm approximation
nodes.statement: For any matrix $B$ of rank at most $k$, $\|A - A_k\|_F \leq \|A - B\|_F$.
assumptions: $A$ is an $n \times d$ matrix
$B$ is any matrix of rank $\leq k$

nodes.statement: Optimal $B$ must have rows that are projections of rows of $A$ onto $B$'s row space $V$. Then $\|A - B\|_F^2$ is the sum of squared distances to $V$, which is minimized by $V_k$ (Theorem 3.1).

nodes.name: Orthogonality of left singular vectors
nodes.statement: The left singular vectors $\mathbf{u}_1, \ldots, \mathbf{u}_r$ are pairwise orthogonal.
assumptions: $A$ is an $n \times d$ matrix with SVD $\sum_i \sigma_i \mathbf{u}_i \mathbf{v}_i^T$
conclusions: $\mathbf{u}_i^T \mathbf{u}_j = 0$ for $i \neq j$

nodes.statement: Assume for contradiction $\mathbf{u}_i^T \mathbf{u}_j = \delta > 0$. Perturb $\mathbf{v}_i' = (\mathbf{v}_i + \epsilon \mathbf{v}_j)/|\mathbf{v}_i + \epsilon \mathbf{v}_j|$. Show $|A\mathbf{v}_i'| > \sigma_i$ for small $\epsilon$, contradicting the definition of $\sigma_i$.

nodes.name: 2-norm of $A - A_k$
assumptions: $A$ has SVD $\sum_{i=1}^r \sigma_i \mathbf{u}_i \mathbf{v}_i^T$
$A_k = \sum_{i=1}^k \sigma_i \mathbf{u}_i \mathbf{v}_i^T$

nodes.statement: Write $\mathbf{v} = \sum c_j \mathbf{v}_j$. Then $|(A - A_k)\mathbf{v}| = \sqrt{\sum_{i=k+1}^r c_i^2 \sigma_i^2}$. Maximized when $c_{k+1} = 1$, rest zero.

nodes.name: Best rank-$k$ spectral norm approximation
nodes.statement: For any matrix $B$ of rank at most $k$, $\|A - A_k\|_2 \leq \|A - B\|_2$.
assumptions: $A$ is an $n \times d$ matrix
$B$ is any matrix of rank $\leq k$

nodes.statement: The null space of $B$ has dimension $\geq d - k$. By dimension argument, there exists unit $\mathbf{z} \in \mathrm{Null}(B) \cap \mathrm{span}(\mathbf{v}_1, \ldots, \mathbf{v}_{k+1})$. Then $\|A - B\|_2^2 \geq |A\mathbf{z}|^2 \geq \sigma_{k+1}^2$.

nodes.name: Analog of eigenvalue equations
nodes.statement: $A\mathbf{v}_i = \sigma_i \mathbf{u}_i$ and $A^T \mathbf{u}_i = \sigma_i \mathbf{v}_i$.
assumptions: $A = \sum_i \sigma_i \mathbf{u}_i \mathbf{v}_i^T$ is the SVD of $A$
conclusions: $A\mathbf{v}_i = \sigma_i \mathbf{u}_i$
$A^T \mathbf{u}_i = \sigma_i \mathbf{v}_i$

nodes.statement: First equation follows from definition of $\mathbf{u}_i$. For the second, $A^T \mathbf{u}_i = \sum_j \sigma_j \mathbf{v}_j \mathbf{u}_j^T \mathbf{u}_i = \sigma_i \mathbf{v}_i$ by orthonormality of $\mathbf{u}_j$.

nodes.name: Power method convergence
nodes.statement: Let $\mathbf{x}$ be a unit vector with $|\mathbf{x}^T \mathbf{v}_1| \geq \delta$. After $k = \frac{\ln(1/\epsilon\delta)}{2\epsilon}$ iterations of the power method, $\mathbf{w} = (A^T A)^k \mathbf{x}/|(A^T A)^k \mathbf{x}|$ has component at most $\epsilon$ perpendicular to the space $V$ of singular vectors with singular values $> (1-\epsilon)\sigma_1$.
assumptions: $A$ is an $n \times d$ matrix
$\mathbf{x}$ is a unit vector with $|\mathbf{x}^T \mathbf{v}_1| \geq \delta > 0$
conclusions: After $k = \ln(1/\epsilon\delta)/(2\epsilon)$ iterations, $\mathbf{w}$ has component $\leq \epsilon$ perpendicular to $V$

nodes.statement: Expand $\mathbf{x} = \sum c_i \mathbf{v}_i$. Then $(A^T A)^k \mathbf{x} = \sum \sigma_i^{2k} c_i \mathbf{v}_i$. The perpendicular component ratio is $\leq (1-\epsilon)^{2k}/\delta \leq e^{-2k\epsilon}/\delta = \epsilon$.

nodes.name: Random vector has nontrivial projection
nodes.statement: If $\mathbf{y}$ is a unit-variance spherical Gaussian in $\mathbb{R}^d$ and $\mathbf{x} = \mathbf{y}/|\mathbf{y}|$, then for any unit $\mathbf{v}$: $\mathrm{Pr}(|\mathbf{x}^T \mathbf{v}| \leq \frac{1}{20\sqrt{d}}) \leq \frac{1}{10} + 3e^{-d/96}$.
assumptions: $\mathbf{y} \sim N(\mathbf{0}, I_d)$
$\mathbf{x} = \mathbf{y}/|\mathbf{y}|$
$\mathbf{v}$ is any unit vector
conclusions: $\mathrm{Pr}(|\mathbf{x}^T \mathbf{v}| \leq \frac{1}{20\sqrt{d}}) \leq \frac{1}{10} + 3e^{-d/96}$

nodes.statement: Use Gaussian Annulus Theorem (Thm 2.9) to bound $\mathrm{Pr}(|\mathbf{y}| \geq 2\sqrt{d})$. Then $\mathbf{y}^T \mathbf{v}$ is a unit Gaussian, so $\mathrm{Pr}(|\mathbf{y}^T \mathbf{v}| \leq 1/10) \leq 1/10$.

nodes.name: Best-fit line passes through centroid
nodes.statement: The best-fit line (minimizing sum of squared perpendicular distances) of a set of data points must pass through the centroid of the points.
assumptions: A set of data points in $\mathbb{R}^d$
conclusions: The best-fit line passes through the centroid

nodes.statement: Center data so centroid is $\mathbf{0}$. If line $\ell = \{\mathbf{a} + \lambda \mathbf{v}\}$ with $\mathbf{a} \neq \mathbf{0}$, the sum of squared distances includes $n|\mathbf{a}|^2 > 0$, so the line through the origin is strictly better.

nodes.name: Best-fit affine subspace passes through centroid
nodes.statement: The $k$-dimensional affine space minimizing the sum of squared perpendicular distances to the data points must pass through the centroid.
assumptions: A set of data points in $\mathbb{R}^d$
conclusions: The best-fit $k$-dimensional affine space passes through the centroid

nodes.statement: Similar to Lemma 3.13; replace $(\mathbf{v} \cdot \mathbf{a}_i)^2$ with $\sum_{j=1}^k (\mathbf{v}_j \cdot \mathbf{a}_i)^2$ using an orthonormal basis of the subspace.

nodes.name: Projection of spherical Gaussian
nodes.statement: The projection of a $d$-dimensional spherical Gaussian with center $\mu$ and std dev $\sigma$ onto a $k$-dimensional subspace $V$ is a spherical Gaussian with the same standard deviation.
assumptions: $p$ is a $d$-dim spherical Gaussian with center $\mu$, std dev $\sigma$
$V$ is a $k$-dimensional subspace
conclusions: The projected density is a $k$-dim spherical Gaussian with std dev $\sigma$

nodes.statement: Rotate so $V$ is spanned by first $k$ coordinates. Integrate out remaining coordinates: $c e^{-|\mathbf{x}' - \mu'|^2/(2\sigma^2)} \int e^{-|\mathbf{x}'' - \mu''|^2/(2\sigma^2)} d\mathbf{x}'' = c' e^{-|\mathbf{x}' - \mu'|^2/(2\sigma^2)}$.

nodes.name: Best-fit line for a spherical Gaussian
nodes.statement: For a spherical Gaussian with center $\mu \neq \mathbf{0}$, the unique best-fit 1-dimensional subspace is the line through $\mu$ and the origin. If $\mu = \mathbf{0}$, any line through the origin is best-fit.
assumptions: $p$ is a spherical Gaussian with center $\mu$
conclusions: Best-fit line is through $\mu$ and the origin (unique if $\mu \neq \mathbf{0}$)

nodes.statement: Compute $E_{\mathbf{x} \sim p}[(\mathbf{v}^T \mathbf{x})^2] = \sigma^2 + (\mathbf{v}^T \mu)^2$. This is maximized when $\mathbf{v}$ is aligned with $\mu$.

nodes.name: Best-fit subspace for a spherical Gaussian
nodes.statement: For a spherical Gaussian with center $\mu$, a $k$-dimensional subspace is a best-fit subspace if and only if it contains $\mu$.
assumptions: $p$ is a spherical Gaussian with center $\mu$
conclusions: $V$ is a best-fit $k$-dim subspace iff $\mu \in V$

nodes.statement: By Lemma 3.16, the best-fit line must pass through $\mu$. After projecting perpendicular to it, the mean becomes $\mathbf{0}$ and any additional directions are equally good.

nodes.name: SVD finds centers of Gaussian mixture
nodes.statement: If $p$ is a mixture of $k$ spherical Gaussians, the best-fit $k$-dimensional subspace contains the centers. If the means are linearly independent, this subspace is unique.
assumptions: $p = \sum_{i=1}^k w_i p_i$ is a mixture of $k$ spherical Gaussians
conclusions: The best-fit $k$-dim subspace contains all $k$ centers
Unique if means are linearly independent

nodes.statement: Write $E_{\mathbf{x} \sim p}(|\mathrm{proj}(\mathbf{x}, V)|^2) = \sum_i w_i E_{\mathbf{x} \sim p_i}(|\mathrm{proj}(\mathbf{x}, V)|^2)$. If $V$ contains all centers, each term is individually maximized by Lemma 3.17.

nodes.name: Approximate max-cut via SVD
nodes.statement: Given a directed graph $G(V, E)$, a cut of size at least the maximum cut minus $O(n^2/\sqrt{k})$ can be computed in time polynomial in $n$ for any fixed $k$.
assumptions: $G$ is an $n$-node directed graph
$k$ is a fixed constant
conclusions: A cut within additive $O(n^2/\sqrt{k})$ of the max-cut can be found in $n^{O(k)}$ time

nodes.name: Power method for SVD
nodes.statement: Pick random $\mathbf{x}$, repeatedly compute $\mathbf{x} \leftarrow A^T A \mathbf{x}$ (as right-to-left sparse matrix-vector products) and normalize. Converges to the top singular vector $\mathbf{v}_1$.

nodes.name: SVD-based approximate max-cut
nodes.statement: Compute rank-$k$ SVD $A_k$. Round coordinates of $\mathbf{u}_i, \mathbf{v}_i$ to multiples of $1/(nk^2)$. Use dynamic programming over $\tilde{\mathbf{w}}(S)$ vectors to find $S$ maximizing $\sum_i \sigma_i \mathbf{u}_i(S) \mathbf{v}_i(\bar{S})$.
input: Adjacency matrix $A$ of a directed graph

nodes.name: First singular vector definition
nodes.statement: $\mathbf{v}_1 = \arg \max_{|\mathbf{v}|=1} |A \mathbf{v}|$

nodes.name: Subsequent singular vector definition
nodes.statement: $\mathbf{v}_k = \arg \max_{\mathbf{v} \perp \mathbf{v}_1, \ldots, \mathbf{v}_{k-1},\, |\mathbf{v}|=1} |A \mathbf{v}|$

nodes.name: Pythagorean decomposition for projections
nodes.statement: $a_{i1}^2 + a_{i2}^2 + \cdots + a_{id}^2 = (\text{length of projection})^2 + (\text{distance to line})^2$

nodes.name: Sum of squared projections equals $|A\mathbf{v}|^2$
nodes.statement: $\sum_{i=1}^n (\mathbf{a}_i \cdot \mathbf{v})^2 = |A \mathbf{v}|^2$

nodes.name: Left singular vector definition
nodes.statement: $\mathbf{u}_i = \frac{1}{\sigma_i(A)} A \mathbf{v}_i$

nodes.name: SVD sum form
nodes.statement: $A = \sum_{i=1}^r \sigma_i \mathbf{u}_i \mathbf{v}_i^T$

nodes.name: Frobenius norm definition
nodes.statement: $\|A\|_F = \sqrt{\sum_{j,k} a_{jk}^2}$

nodes.name: Frobenius norm via singular values
nodes.statement: $\sum_{j=1}^n |\mathbf{a}_j|^2 = \sum_{i=1}^r |A \mathbf{v}_i|^2 = \sum_{i=1}^r \sigma_i^2(A) = \|A\|_F^2$

nodes.name: Rank-$k$ truncated SVD
nodes.statement: $A_k = \sum_{i=1}^k \sigma_i \mathbf{u}_i \mathbf{v}_i^T$

nodes.name: Spectral norm definition
nodes.statement: $\|A\|_2 = \max_{|\mathbf{x}| \leq 1} |A \mathbf{x}| = \sigma_1(A)$

nodes.name: Perturbation vector for orthogonality proof
nodes.statement: $\mathbf{v}_i' = \frac{\mathbf{v}_i + \epsilon \mathbf{v}_j}{|\mathbf{v}_i + \epsilon \mathbf{v}_j|}$

nodes.name: Eigenvalue equations for singular vectors
nodes.statement: $A \mathbf{v}_i = \sigma_i \mathbf{u}_i$ and $A^T \mathbf{u}_i = \sigma_i \mathbf{v}_i$

nodes.name: $A^T A$ in singular vector basis
nodes.statement: $A^T A = \sum_{i} \sigma_i^2 \mathbf{v}_i \mathbf{v}_i^T$

nodes.name: Power of $B = A^T A$
nodes.statement: $B^k = (A^T A)^k = \sum_{i=1}^r \sigma_i^{2k} \mathbf{v}_i \mathbf{v}_i^T$

nodes.name: Power method iterate
nodes.statement: $\mathbf{w} = \frac{(A^T A)^k \mathbf{x}}{|(A^T A)^k \mathbf{x}|}$

nodes.name: Perpendicular component decay bound
nodes.statement: $\frac{(1-\epsilon)^{2k}}{\delta} \leq \frac{e^{-2k\epsilon}}{\delta} = \epsilon$

nodes.name: Gaussian projected density
nodes.statement: $c e^{-|\mathbf{x}' - \mu'|^2/(2\sigma^2)} \int e^{-|\mathbf{x}'' - \mu''|^2/(2\sigma^2)} d\mathbf{x}'' = c' e^{-|\mathbf{x}' - \mu'|^2/(2\sigma^2)}$

nodes.name: Bias-variance decomposition for best-fit line
nodes.statement: $E_{\mathbf{x} \sim p}[(\mathbf{v}^T \mathbf{x})^2] = \sigma^2 + (\mathbf{v}^T \mu)^2$

nodes.name: Mixture best-fit decomposition
nodes.statement: $E_{\mathbf{x} \sim p}(|\mathrm{proj}(\mathbf{x}, V)|^2) = \sum_{i=1}^k w_i E_{\mathbf{x} \sim p_i}(|\mathrm{proj}(\mathbf{x}, V)|^2)$

nodes.name: Max-cut objective in matrix form
nodes.statement: $\sum_{i,j} x_i (1-x_j) a_{ij} = \mathbf{x}^T A (\mathbf{1} - \mathbf{x})$

nodes.name: SVD approximation error bound for max-cut
nodes.statement: $|\mathbf{x}^T (A - A_k)(\mathbf{1} - \mathbf{x})| \leq n \|A - A_k\|_2 \leq \frac{n^2}{\sqrt{k+1}}$

nodes.name: Singular value upper bound
nodes.statement: $(k+1) \sigma_{k+1}^2 \leq \sum_{i=1}^{k+1} \sigma_i^2 \leq \|A\|_F^2 \leq n^2$

nodes.name: Centroid sum-of-squares expansion
nodes.statement: $\sum_{i=1}^n \mathrm{dist}(\mathbf{a}_i, \ell)^2 = \sum_i |\mathbf{a}_i|^2 + n|\mathbf{a}|^2 - \sum_i (\mathbf{v} \cdot \mathbf{a}_i)^2$

nodes.name: Inter-center separation condition
nodes.statement: $\Delta > c d^{1/4} \sigma$ for distance-based clustering; $\Delta > c k^{1/4} \sigma$ suffices after SVD projection

nodes.name: Null space dimension argument
nodes.statement: $\dim(\mathrm{Null}(B)) \geq d - k$, so $\mathrm{Null}(B) \cap \mathrm{span}(\mathbf{v}_1, \ldots, \mathbf{v}_{k+1}) \neq \{\mathbf{0}\}$
Base case: for $k=1$, $V_1 = \mathrm{span}(\mathbf{v}_1)$ is best-fit by definition of $\mathbf{v}_1$.
Inductive hypothesis: assume $V_{k-1}$ is a best-fit $(k-1)$-dimensional subspace.
Let $W$ be any best-fit $k$-dim subspace. Choose orthonormal basis $\mathbf{w}_1, \ldots, \mathbf{w}_k$ of $W$ so that $\mathbf{w}_k \perp \mathbf{v}_1, \ldots, \mathbf{v}_{k-1}$.
By inductive hypothesis, $\sum_{i=1}^{k-1} |A \mathbf{w}_i|^2 \leq \sum_{i=1}^{k-1} |A \mathbf{v}_i|^2$ since $V_{k-1}$ is optimal.
Since $\mathbf{w}_k \perp \mathbf{v}_1, \ldots, \mathbf{v}_{k-1}$, by definition of $\mathbf{v}_k$ we have $|A \mathbf{w}_k|^2 \leq |A \mathbf{v}_k|^2$.
Adding: $\sum_{i=1}^k |A \mathbf{w}_i|^2 \leq \sum_{i=1}^k |A \mathbf{v}_i|^2$, so $V_k$ is at least as good as $W$.
The singular vectors $\mathbf{v}_1, \ldots, \mathbf{v}_r$ span the row space of $A$.

For each row $\mathbf{a}_j$, since $\mathbf{a}_j \cdot \mathbf{v} = 0$ for all $\mathbf{v} \perp \mathbf{v}_1, \ldots, \mathbf{v}_r$, we get $\sum_{i=1}^r (\mathbf{a}_j \cdot \mathbf{v}_i)^2 = |\mathbf{a}_j|^2$.
Sum over all rows: $\sum_{j=1}^n |\mathbf{a}_j|^2 = \sum_{i=1}^r \sum_{j=1}^n (\mathbf{a}_j \cdot \mathbf{v}_i)^2 = \sum_{i=1}^r |A \mathbf{v}_i|^2 = \sum_{i=1}^r \sigma_i^2 = \|A\|_F^2$.
If $A = B$ then clearly $A\mathbf{v} = B\mathbf{v}$ for all $\mathbf{v}$.
Conversely, let $\mathbf{e}_i$ be the $i$-th standard basis vector. Then $A \mathbf{e}_i$ is the $i$-th column of $A$.
Since $A \mathbf{e}_i = B \mathbf{e}_i$ for all $i$, all columns match, so $A = B$.
Compute $\sum_{i=1}^r \sigma_i \mathbf{u}_i \mathbf{v}_i^T \mathbf{v}_j = \sigma_j \mathbf{u}_j$ by orthonormality of $\mathbf{v}_i$.
By definition $A \mathbf{v}_j = \sigma_j \mathbf{u}_j$, so $A \mathbf{v}_j = (\sum_i \sigma_i \mathbf{u}_i \mathbf{v}_i^T) \mathbf{v}_j$ for each $j$.
Any $\mathbf{v}$ can be written as a linear combination of $\mathbf{v}_j$ plus a component perpendicular to all $\mathbf{v}_j$; both sides annihilate the perpendicular component.
By Lemma 3.3, since $A \mathbf{v} = (\sum_i \sigma_i \mathbf{u}_i \mathbf{v}_i^T) \mathbf{v}$ for all $\mathbf{v}$, we conclude $A = \sum_i \sigma_i \mathbf{u}_i \mathbf{v}_i^T$.
The projection of a row $\mathbf{a}$ onto $V_k$ is $\sum_{i=1}^k (\mathbf{a} \cdot \mathbf{v}_i) \mathbf{v}_i^T$ since $\mathbf{v}_i$ are orthonormal.
The matrix of projected rows is $\sum_{i=1}^k A \mathbf{v}_i \mathbf{v}_i^T = \sum_{i=1}^k \sigma_i \mathbf{u}_i \mathbf{v}_i^T = A_k$.
Let $B$ minimize $\|A - B\|_F^2$ among rank $\leq k$ matrices; let $V$ be the row space of $B$.
Each row of $B$ must be the projection of the corresponding row of $A$ onto $V$, otherwise replacing it with the projection reduces the error while keeping rank $\leq k$.
So $\|A - B\|_F^2$ equals the sum of squared distances of rows of $A$ to $V$. By Theorem 3.1, $V_k$ minimizes this, hence $\|A - A_k\|_F \leq \|A - B\|_F$.
Assume for contradiction that $\mathbf{u}_i^T \mathbf{u}_j = \delta > 0$ for the smallest $i$ with some non-orthogonal $\mathbf{u}_j$, $j > i$.

Define $\mathbf{v}_i' = (\mathbf{v}_i + \epsilon \mathbf{v}_j)/|\mathbf{v}_i + \epsilon \mathbf{v}_j|$. Then $A \mathbf{v}_i' = (\sigma_i \mathbf{u}_i + \epsilon \sigma_j \mathbf{u}_j)/\sqrt{1 + \epsilon^2}$.
The component along $\mathbf{u}_i$ is $(\sigma_i + \epsilon \sigma_j \delta)(1 - \epsilon^2/2) > \sigma_i$ for small $\epsilon$.
This contradicts $\sigma_i = \max_{\mathbf{v} \perp \mathbf{v}_1,\ldots,\mathbf{v}_{i-1}} |A\mathbf{v}|$ since $\mathbf{v}_i'$ is perpendicular to $\mathbf{v}_1, \ldots, \mathbf{v}_{i-1}$.
$A - A_k = \sum_{i=k+1}^r \sigma_i \mathbf{u}_i \mathbf{v}_i^T$. Write $\mathbf{v} = \sum_{j=1}^r c_j \mathbf{v}_j$.
Then $|(A - A_k) \mathbf{v}| = |\sum_{i=k+1}^r c_i \sigma_i \mathbf{u}_i| = \sqrt{\sum_{i=k+1}^r c_i^2 \sigma_i^2}$ by orthonormality of $\mathbf{u}_i$.
Subject to $\sum c_i^2 = 1$, maximized when $c_{k+1} = 1$ and all other $c_i = 0$, giving $\|A - A_k\|_2^2 = \sigma_{k+1}^2$.
If $A$ has rank $\leq k$ the result is trivial. Otherwise, $\|A - A_k\|_2^2 = \sigma_{k+1}^2$ by Lemma 3.8.

$\mathrm{Null}(B)$ has dimension $\geq d - k$ and $\mathrm{span}(\mathbf{v}_1, \ldots, \mathbf{v}_{k+1})$ has dimension $k+1$. Since $(d-k) + (k+1) > d$, their intersection contains a nonzero vector $\mathbf{z}$.
Scale $\mathbf{z}$ to unit length. Then $\|A - B\|_2^2 \geq |(A-B)\mathbf{z}|^2 = |A\mathbf{z}|^2$ since $B\mathbf{z} = 0$.
Since $\mathbf{z} \in \mathrm{span}(\mathbf{v}_1, \ldots, \mathbf{v}_{k+1})$, $|A\mathbf{z}|^2 = \sum_{i=1}^{k+1} \sigma_i^2 (\mathbf{v}_i^T \mathbf{z})^2 \geq \sigma_{k+1}^2$.
First equation: $A \mathbf{v}_i = \sigma_i \mathbf{u}_i$ follows directly from the definition $\mathbf{u}_i = A \mathbf{v}_i / \sigma_i$.

From SVD: $A^T = \sum_j \sigma_j \mathbf{v}_j \mathbf{u}_j^T$, so $A^T \mathbf{u}_i = \sum_j \sigma_j \mathbf{v}_j (\mathbf{u}_j^T \mathbf{u}_i) = \sigma_i \mathbf{v}_i$ by orthonormality of $\mathbf{u}_j$.
Write $\mathbf{x} = \sum_{i=1}^d c_i \mathbf{v}_i$ with $|c_1| \geq \delta$. Then $(A^T A)^k \mathbf{x} = \sum_{i=1}^d \sigma_i^{2k} c_i \mathbf{v}_i$.
The squared length is $|(A^T A)^k \mathbf{x}|^2 = \sum_i \sigma_i^{4k} c_i^2 \geq \sigma_1^{4k} \delta^2$.
The perpendicular component (from singular values $< (1-\epsilon)\sigma_1$) satisfies $\sum_{i=m+1}^d \sigma_i^{4k} c_i^2 \leq (1-\epsilon)^{4k} \sigma_1^{4k}$.
After normalizing, the perpendicular component has length $\leq (1-\epsilon)^{2k}/\delta \leq e^{-2k\epsilon}/\delta = \epsilon$ for $k = \ln(1/(\epsilon\delta))/(2\epsilon)$.
By the Gaussian Annulus Theorem (Thm 2.9 with $\beta = \sqrt{d}$), $\mathrm{Pr}(|\mathbf{y}| \geq 2\sqrt{d}) \leq 3 e^{-d/96}$.
$\mathbf{y}^T \mathbf{v}$ is a standard Gaussian with density $\leq 1/\sqrt{2\pi} \leq 1/2$, so $\mathrm{Pr}(|\mathbf{y}^T \mathbf{v}| \leq 1/10) \leq 1/10$.
Combining: if $|\mathbf{y}| \leq 2\sqrt{d}$ and $|\mathbf{y}^T \mathbf{v}| > 1/10$, then $|\mathbf{x}^T \mathbf{v}| = |\mathbf{y}^T \mathbf{v}|/|\mathbf{y}| > 1/(20\sqrt{d})$.
Center the data so the centroid is $\mathbf{0}$, i.e., $\sum_i \mathbf{a}_i = \mathbf{0}$.

Write the line as $\ell = \{\mathbf{a} + \lambda \mathbf{v}\}$ where $\mathbf{a} \perp \mathbf{v}$. Expand: $\sum_i \mathrm{dist}(\mathbf{a}_i, \ell)^2 = \sum_i |\mathbf{a}_i|^2 + n|\mathbf{a}|^2 - \sum_i (\mathbf{v} \cdot \mathbf{a}_i)^2$ using $\sum_i \mathbf{a}_i = \mathbf{0}$.
The term $n|\mathbf{a}|^2 > 0$ when $\mathbf{a} \neq \mathbf{0}$, so the line through the origin ($\mathbf{a} = \mathbf{0}$) gives a strictly smaller sum. Contradiction.
Rotate coordinates so $V$ is spanned by the first $k$ coordinate vectors. The Gaussian remains spherical with std dev $\sigma$.
The projected density at $\mathbf{x}' = (x_1, \ldots, x_k)$ is $c e^{-|\mathbf{x}' - \mu'|^2/(2\sigma^2)} \int e^{-|\mathbf{x}'' - \mu''|^2/(2\sigma^2)} d\mathbf{x}''$.
The integral over $\mathbf{x}''$ is a constant, so the result is $c' e^{-|\mathbf{x}' - \mu'|^2/(2\sigma^2)}$, a spherical Gaussian with std dev $\sigma$.

Decompose $\mathbf{x} = (\mathbf{x} - \mu) + \mu$. Then $E[(\mathbf{v}^T \mathbf{x})^2] = E[(\mathbf{v}^T(\mathbf{x}-\mu))^2] + 2(\mathbf{v}^T \mu) E[\mathbf{v}^T(\mathbf{x}-\mu)] + (\mathbf{v}^T \mu)^2$.
The cross term vanishes since $E[\mathbf{v}^T(\mathbf{x}-\mu)] = 0$. The variance term is $\sigma^2$ for any unit $\mathbf{v}$ (spherical symmetry).
So $E[(\mathbf{v}^T \mathbf{x})^2] = \sigma^2 + (\mathbf{v}^T \mu)^2$, maximized when $\mathbf{v} = \mu/|\mu|$. Unique if $\mu \neq \mathbf{0}$.
If $\mu = \mathbf{0}$, by symmetry any subspace is equally good.
If $\mu \neq \mathbf{0}$, the best-fit line must pass through $\mu$ by Lemma 3.16. The best-fit $k$-dim subspace must contain this line.
After projecting perpendicular to $\mu$, the Gaussian has mean $\mathbf{0}$, so any additional directions are equally good. Hence any $k$-dim subspace containing $\mu$ is best-fit.
Write $E_{\mathbf{x} \sim p}(|\mathrm{proj}(\mathbf{x},V)|^2) = \sum_{i=1}^k w_i E_{\mathbf{x} \sim p_i}(|\mathrm{proj}(\mathbf{x},V)|^2)$ by linearity of expectation.
If $V$ contains all centers $\mu_1, \ldots, \mu_k$, then by Lemma 3.17 each $E_{\mathbf{x} \sim p_i}(|\mathrm{proj}(\mathbf{x},V)|^2)$ is individually maximized.
Thus the entire weighted sum is maximized, proving the best-fit $k$-dim subspace contains all centers.
Item 1: For 0-1 vectors $\mathbf{x}$ and $\mathbf{1}-\mathbf{x}$ of length $\leq \sqrt{n}$, $|\mathbf{x}^T(A - A_k)(\mathbf{1}-\mathbf{x})| \leq n \|A - A_k\|_2$.
By Lemma 3.8, $\|A - A_k\|_2 = \sigma_{k+1}$. From $(k+1)\sigma_{k+1}^2 \leq \|A\|_F^2 \leq n^2$, we get $\sigma_{k+1} \leq n/\sqrt{k+1}$.
Item 2: Round $\mathbf{u}_i, \mathbf{v}_i$ coordinates to multiples of $1/(nk^2)$. Dynamic programming over $\tilde{\mathbf{w}}(S)$ vectors finds near-optimal $S$.
The list of distinct $\tilde{\mathbf{w}}(S)$ has size at most $(2n^{3/2} k^2)^{2k}$, polynomial in $n$ for fixed $k$.
Rounding error: $|\sum_i \sigma_i \tilde{\mathbf{u}}_i(S) \tilde{\mathbf{v}}_i(\bar{S}) - \sum_i \sigma_i \mathbf{u}_i(S) \mathbf{v}_i(\bar{S})| \leq 3k \sigma_1 \sqrt{n}/k^2 \leq n^2/k$.
